equations.meaning: Head arc equation and validity domain
Equivalent head ODE, sign fixed by inward motion
Strict positivity only when b,r>0 and 0<delta<pi
Existence needs endpoint sign condition as well as monotonicity
Differentiate constant squared rod length; two-times factor cancels

equations.latex: \boxed{\omega_i=\frac{\mathbf d_i^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\tau(\theta_{i-1})}{D_i}\omega_{i-1}},\quad D_i=\mathbf d_i^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\tau(\theta_i)=\tfrac12\frac{\partial F}{\partial\delta}>0,\quad \mathbf V_i=\boldsymbol\tau(\theta_i)\omega_i,\quad U_i=\|\mathbf V_i\|
equations.meaning: Recurrence and positive denominator on certified branch; values have different units as declared in symbol table
With frozen p=.55m, implies head theta>16pi until300s

steps: Differentiate X componentwise using the product rule.
Expand squared tangent norm: cross terms cancel and cos²+sin²=1, obtaining b²(1+theta²).
Use d[theta sqrt(1+theta²)]/dtheta=sqrt(1+theta²)+theta²/sqrt(1+theta²) and d asinh(theta)/dtheta=1/sqrt(1+theta²).
The sum times b/2 is b sqrt(1+theta²); value at zero vanishes.
Constant speed along the curve makes traversed length v0*t.
Inward travel subtracts arc length from S(theta_init).
Differentiate using the chain rule: -Sprime(theta0)*omega0=v0; divide by positive b sqrt(1+theta0²).
Rotate previous handle to angle0 without changing Euclidean distance. Radii are r and r+b*delta.
Squared distance equals r²+(r+b*delta)²-2r(r+b*delta)cos(delta).
Regroup as (b*delta)²+2r(r+b*delta)(1-cos(delta)).
Use 1-cos(delta)=2sin²(delta/2); subtract ell². This avoids subtracting nearly equal O(r²) terms.
Let d_i=X_i-X_i-1. Differentiate d_i dot d_i=L_i²: 2d_i dot(V_i-V_i-1)=0.
Apply chain rule V_i=tau(theta_i)*omega_i; rearrange coefficients of omega_i.
With previous handle fixed, derivative of squared distance with respect to delta is 2d_i dot tau(theta_i).
Use strict Fdelta>0 on the certified interval; division is justified analytically. A finite-precision threshold is still necessary for conditioning.
S is continuous and strictly increasing because Sprime=b sqrt(1+theta²)>0.
Right side S(theta_init)-v0t lies in(0,S(theta_init)] so a unique head angle in(0,theta_init] exists by the intermediate value theorem.
Differentiation gives omega0<0; t=0 returns theta_init. The positive-radius domain ends at the origin, not beyond.
F is continuous on[0,pi]. Its lower endpoint is strictly negative and upper endpoint strictly positive under the stated chord bound.
On(0,pi), every term of Fdelta is nonnegative and 2b²delta is strictly positive. Thus F is strictly increasing.
The intermediate value theorem gives exactly one root delta* in(0,pi). No smaller positive root exists by monotonicity, so it is the first outward root.
No claim is made about branches outside pi or that no roots exist if the upper sign test fails.
For u>=0, u<=sqrt(1+u²)<=u+1; integrate to bound S(32pi) from below and S(16pi) from above.
The resulting difference is105.6pi-4.4>300m (already follows from pi>3). Thus at300s the head theta remains>16pi and radius>4.4m; earlier radii are larger.
Induct along the outward chain: every previous radius is>4.4m. Hence 2r+b*pi>9.075m>2.86m, certifying each neighbour bracket throughout the continuous interval.
At each finite stage the implicit-function derivative Fdelta is positive, so differentiability and the velocity recurrence hold locally; no uniform floating-point condition-number bound is asserted.
